schema_version: v0 — component-charter shape; migrates into the intention envelope when MAP.md Q6 lands
what: The device that HOLDS aider in-process so it can do build typing on CC's behalf. It is a Cairn device — its own process, its own charter, instance 0 — that imports a foreign program (aider, a git checkout at ~/dev/src/aider, v0.86.3.dev HEAD 5dc9490bb) and drives it through its Python API. Three things make it a device rather than a wrapper. FIRST, THE INTERCEPTOR: aider reaches every model it will ever reach through exactly one call site, `res = litellm.completion(**kwargs)` in Model.send_completion (measured 2026-08-16 by grep over the whole tree — one chat-completion call site, every coder and every edit format and every retry path funnelling through it). the interception point is `sys.modules['litellm']` — a surface module installed there BEFORE aider is imported, so the real litellm is never imported at all. It answers the eight callables aider touches (completion, completion_cost, model_cost, get_model_info, validate_environment, token_counter, encode, transcription — the last on the voice path only, and it refuses) plus the 23 exception classes aider's `EXCEPTIONS` list names, and translates completion into `inference_domain.domain.resolve`. THE SLOT WAS THE CHART'S ANSWER AND IT WAS MEASURED WRONG DURING THE BUILD: survey held that replacing aider's lazy `LazyLiteLLM` slot before first attribute access would suffice, because it had grepped `litellm\.` — which finds attribute ACCESS and is structurally blind to `import` statements. `aider/exceptions.py` does a bare `import litellm` at lines 68 and 87, and `simple_send_with_retries` constructs `LiteLLMExceptions()` on EVERY call, so the real module would have loaded on the hot path with the slot dutifully replaced. Pre-empting `sys.modules` covers both roads and is the smaller change — `LazyLiteLLM` keeps working untouched, since its `importlib.import_module` of that name now returns ours. SECOND, THE FENCE: the same object refuses by model name and provider at the seam, so the ask cannot widen — and because the injection point and the fence are one object, they cannot drift out of agreement with each other. THIRD, THE TRANSLATION: its input is a cast ticket's berthed chart chain plus ONE decompose piece — survey holdings become the file list, constrain bounds plus the piece become the prompt, the ticket's proofs become aider's test loop — and its output enters proven-space through the UNCHANGED physics: proofs twice, tester seal, verdict artifact, clearance gate. It has no HTTP face, no route, no port, no server (one web server), and it never runs aider as a subprocess (a subprocess imports nothing and would slip the sieve while breaching the law the sieve enforces). AND THE REPO MAP IS OFF, WHICH IS PART OF THE TRANSLATION AND NOT A PERFORMANCE SETTING. aider's `map_tokens` walks the whole repository and splices a ranked digest of it into the prompt — content assembled by the HELD PROGRAM, after translate.py has finished counting spans. So falsifier clause (7) could be violated while the instrument that watches clause (7) reported zero untraceable spans, because the violation happens downstream of the only thing that can see it. `Brief.map_tokens = 0` closes it at the one place it can be closed, with a tooth that reds if it moves. It is also Law 1 twice over: the chart chain already settled which files a piece touches (survey's holdings, constrain's bounds), so a repo map is aider re-deriving the settled by heuristic. MEASURED, NOT REASONED — the first live fire died in `repomap.get_ranked_tags` on `import networkx`, a module this device's own venv closure had correctly measured as lazy-only and therefore never installed; the traceback is what surfaced the prompt hole, and installing networkx would have hidden it. FOURTH, SINCE 2026-08-17, THE DRIVER — and it is what turned this device from a description of an offload into one. `driver.drive_brief` takes a Brief, runs the real aider Coder inside the shim's venv interpreter, and comes back as SERIALIZABLE DATA: the files as they stood before, the files as they stand after, what aider reported it edited, how many asks the fence allowed, and any error, appended to ~/.cairn/devices/aider_shim/0/drives.jsonl. The interpreter boundary is why the result is data and never a live Coder — the loop is in-process with aider and out-of-process from CC at the same time — and the seam across it is a SPEC STRING rather than a callable: a "module:attr" or "/abs/file.py:attr" resolved inside the venv, because a callable cannot be JSON. That string is also the only window in which the environment can be arranged BEFORE `aider.models` is imported, which is what made the network scar below findable at all. `driver.survival` is the reader that answers, per file, whether the drive's edit is still what the drive left.
why: THE LIVED SYMPTOM: every line of code in this system is typed by the most expensive model available, including the lines whose shape was already settled three chart stages earlier. A decompose piece that says what to build, a constrain bound that says what is out, and a proof that says when it is right together describe the work closely enough that the typing is transcription — and transcription is what a 30B coder model on a box we already own is for. The offload is not about cost alone; it is about WHERE the expensive resolver is spent (Law 1: on the novel, not on re-deriving the settled). THE OTHER HALF OF THE WHY IS THAT THIS IS AN EXPERIMENT AND IT IS ALLOWED TO FAIL. The claim under test is that a cheaper model, handed a chart chain, can produce work that passes the same gates unchanged. If it cannot, the honest outcome is a red measured against a baseline, not a relaxed gate — which is exactly why constrain put 'relaxing, bypassing or special-casing any gate the output must pass' out of bounds. The unchanged physics IS the experiment. And it rehearses the thing that comes after: this is the first component whose OUTPUT is judged rather than whose behaviour is, which is the shape the cocoon needs.
invoke: import: `from cairn.devices.aider_shim import shim` (the fenced surface) or `from cairn.devices.aider_shim import driver` (the builder loop: `drive_brief(brief)` -> a DriveResult, recorded; `drives(path)` and `survival(rec)` read it back). Prove: `cairn test cairn/devices/aider_shim` for all six, or one at a time — `python3 cairn/devices/aider_shim/proofs/test_driver.py` (exit 0 = green) — or under the tester with `cairn test --netns --seal <path>`, which is the only hand that may mint a validation. The proofs need no network by construction — every model call in a proof goes to a fixture; the only real dial is the live fire, which is not a proof.
node_class: device — its own process, holding a foreign program in-process. Instance 0 is the singleton and is not an exemption. Its runtime state (what it drove, what it spent, what came back) berths at ~/.cairn/devices/aider_shim/0/ and never in class-space.
entry: FRESH design; the foreign program is HELD, not grafted. aider's bytes stay at ~/dev/src/aider, unmodified — modifying it is out of bounds, because a change we make there is unversioned by us and makes the measurement unrepeatable. What is borrowed is an idea and it is cited rather than copied: aider's own LazyLiteLLM is the pattern that makes the interception clean, and it was written for startup speed, not for us. The seam it accidentally provides is the entire reason this device is small.
state_and_history: compiled to state.json (projected window) + history.json (append-only voyage) beside this charter — the charter-state-history split; this file stays pure intention+why. Runtime state — which pieces were driven, what came back, what it cost — is instance-space at ~/.cairn/devices/aider_shim/0/ and never here.
filed_edges: (a) THE SIEVE IS BLIND HERE AND THE CHARTER SAYS SO RATHER THAN INHERITING A COMFORT. cairn/tools/import_sieve builds its graph over OUR repo's .py files and computes which of OUR modules reach a target. A third-party client imported by a HELD FOREIGN PROGRAM is not in that graph — so the sieve would not have caught aider dialing out, and a green sieve is not evidence about this device's sole-path compliance. The evidence is the fence proof and `interceptor.installed()` — an IDENTITY check (is the module at that name OURS?), not the absence check the chart wrote. The chart's criterion said `'litellm' not in sys.modules` after a driven run, and that instrument would have gone red at the moment the design succeeded, since the whole mechanism is to PUT something there. The distinction is carried to the verdict rather than edited into the berth. This is a second residue beside the subprocess one inference_domain's charter already names, and it is owed a ticket.

(b) TELEMETRY LOADS IN OUR PROCESS. posthog and mixpanel are required at aider's import time via aider/analytics.py (measured 2026-08-16 by AST closure over `from aider.coders import Coder`). Whether they can transmit, and whether a held foreign program with telemetry clients loaded in-process is acceptable as a standing arrangement, is a question NO LAW IN THE CORPUS CURRENTLY ADDRESSES — the sole-path law is about the inference host specifically. It is an escalation to Akien, not a thing to configure around quietly.

(c) ONE PIECE PER INVOCATION IS A DECISION, NOT A DISCOVERY. The ambiguity — whole ticket or one decompose piece — was carried openly from orient through constrain and settled at decompose on three grounds: a piece already carries its own what/why/kind so the prompt has a stated aim without one being invented; triage already produces the order, so a whole-ticket shim would re-derive a sequencing the chain has settled (Law 1's defect); and concentrating a multi-piece build loop here would put complexity in one component, which degrades every tier of Claude (ruled 2026-08-16). It grows into the larger against a measured need, if one appears.

(e) THE REFUSAL'S SHAPE IS CONSTRAINED BY A HANDLER NOBODY KNEW TO WRITE DOWN. The design worried about one absorption path — aider retries its `exceptions_tuple()` with backoff to RETRY_TIMEOUT, so a refusal wearing a litellm error name would burn 60s on a decision that will never change. Parsing aider's actual handlers found a second and worse one sitting beside it: `except AttributeError: return None` in `simple_send_with_retries`, which would turn a refusal into 'the model returned nothing' — silently, with no record and no red. That is falsifier clause (4) reached by a road the charter's prose did not name. The tooth for it is DERIVED, not transcribed: the fence proof parses that function's except-handlers each run and requires AskWidened to be caught by none of them, so it survives aider changing its handlers under us. Recorded here because the lesson generalises past this device — a claim of the form 'X propagates out of foreign code untouched' is a claim ABOUT that code, and the honest instrument reads the code rather than listing what we remember it catching.

(d) THE BASELINE THE FALSIFIER NEEDS DOES NOT EXIST. The ticket compares the shim's CC tool-call count against a direct build's, and nothing counts the calls today — it is a hand's act, as the 2026-08-14 ruling says plainly. The probe carries the shimmed half; the baseline half is owed.

(f) THE PROBE'S MEASURED COLUMN WAS READ OUT OF A KEY THE VERDICT DOOR HAS NEVER WRITTEN, and this edge is filed because the FIX is local while the SHAPE is not. The probe read `artifact['criteria']` and compared outcomes to `'passed'`; the door writes `artifact['verdicts']` with OUTCOMES `('pass','fail')`. Every real artifact therefore yielded zero rows counted and `passed: False` — the measured half of this device's watch structurally dead, reporting green=0 forever underneath a carrier that looked healthy. Seventeen sealed teeth stood over it and none bit, because the proof's FIXTURE hand-wrote the reader's invented shape: a fixture that agrees with the READER instead of with the WRITER proves only that one head agrees with itself, and that is a class of hollow proof the tester cannot detect. Closed here by composing the door (OUTCOMES imported, `verdict_error` asked, one tooth building its artifact THROUGH `write_verdict`), and mutation-validated 3/3. WHAT IS NOT CLOSED: nothing in the corpus reds a proof whose fixture was never checked against the producer it stands for — the survey-floor trouble standing in the inbox today is the same shape at a different seam. Owed a ticket, and it is not this device's to own.

(g) THE DEFAULT ASK-LOG WROTE NOWHERE, AND 24 GREEN TEETH COULD NOT HAVE SAID SO. `drive_brief(log_path=None)` built a SeenLog with `record_path=None` — an in-memory log that died with the venv process — so every ask the fence allowed was recorded correctly and then lost. A FIXTURE THAT SUPPLIES AN ARGUMENT CAN NEVER FALSIFY THE DEFAULT THAT SUPPLIES NONE: every tooth passed a tmp path, so the default was the one arrangement no fixture exercised. The first live fire found it, which is the only thing that could have. Closed by importing the fence's own DEFAULT_RECORD rather than re-spelling the path — two spellings of one path is how a store quietly becomes two — with a tooth that asserts the identity and a mutant that reds when the resolution is removed.

(h) MODEL CONSTRUCTION DIALS THE NETWORK WHEN THE CACHE IS COLD, AND THE FIRST MEASUREMENT SAID OTHERWISE BECAUSE THE CACHE WAS 19 HOURS OLD. aider's ModelInfoManager falls through to a bare `requests.get` against raw.githubusercontent.com/BerriAI/litellm whenever its 24h JSON cache misses — a road the interceptor does not cover, because it is not a litellm call at all. The tooth that 'proved' no network re-staged the model seeding inside its own in-venv script, so it measured the arrangement and not the driver: mutating the driver's real seed line left it green. Closed with a seam that sets HOME to an empty directory (a guaranteed cold cache) and replaces `requests.get` with a recording tripwire, then drives the REAL `drive_brief`. The mutant now reds naming the litellm URL. This is a THIRD residue beside (a): the sieve is blind here for the same reason — a third-party client imported by a held foreign program is not in our import graph.

(i) THE APPRENTICE DID NOT PRODUCE AN EDIT, AND THAT IS RECORDED RATHER THAN ROUTED AROUND. Two live fires against qwen3-coder:30b on hex, on a 13,932-char brief, both returned fenced ```python blocks instead of SEARCH/REPLACE, so aider applied nothing: `aider_reported_edited: []`, no file hash moved, 1 allowed ask, 0 reflections. `edit_format` is pinned to 'diff' (aider defaults a model absent from MODEL_SETTINGS to 'whole'), so the format is asked for and not delivered. The edit-survival watch's first real reading is therefore `not-applied` — the disposition that probe deliberately refuses to collapse into `discarded`, because 'the apprentice is not producing' and 'the apprentice is being overruled' call for opposite decisions from the consumer. Widening the ask cap to buy reflections, or changing the edit format, is a bounds question for Akien (Law 9), not a fix to make unilaterally.
gates: proof gate — proofs/ beside this charter, run by the tester under isolation='netns', run twice, with netns and non-netns outcomes required identical (a proof that passes only outside the netns is reaching the host, and its seal would be a statement about hex's availability rather than about this code). Durability gate: not done until proven AND committed. Money gate: the fence proof, which must red on a widened ask AND must fail if its seen-names log is empty — a green earned because nothing was asked is the hollow green this device is most exposed to.
falsifier: RED on any of: (1) the module at sys.modules['litellm'] after a driven run is not ours — `interceptor.installed()` is False — so the interception did not hold and the sole path is a policy rather than a construction; (2) a model call reaches a provider without passing this device's completion — the fence was bypassed rather than refused, which is the money failure; (3) a widened ask (weak_model or editor_model naming a different model) is served rather than refused; (4) a refusal is absorbed by any handler on aider's own call path — retried to RETRY_TIMEOUT by its exceptions tuple, swallowed by its `except AttributeError: return None`, or smoothed into a generic failure in what this device records (Law 7 at a record of truth); (5) inference_domain acquires a row, field, flag or branch for this consumer — the provider learned about its consumer, which is the ruling of 2026-08-16 and the reason domains exist at all; (6) a proof here passes without the netns and fails with it; (7) a prompt handed to aider contains anything not traceable to a berthed packet field — the chain stopped being the input and the conversation started being it.
how_it_learns: THROUGH ITS PROBE, AND THE PROBE IS THE POINT OF THE DEVICE RATHER THAN AN OBLIGATION ON IT. This device exists to answer a question it cannot answer by running: can a Q4_K_M 30B coder, handed a chart chain, produce work that passes the unchanged physics? Every ticket built through the shim reaches a verdict artifact, and that deposit is the event — no poll. The probe at probes/offload_yield_probe.py carries, per shimmed piece: did it pass the unchanged physics, what did it cost in CC tool calls against the direct-build baseline, and whether CC had to supply context beyond the piece and the bounds (which is what would falsify the one-piece-per-invocation decision in filed edge (c)). It deposits to the hypothesize tree, beside what killed or confirmed each expectation. THE PROBE CARRIES NO AUTHORITY: it deposits and pokes; re-opening a node whose intention did not work is the owner's act (Law 6). The consumer is Akien at triage — offload-more versus pull-back is his call. A SECOND PROBE SINCE 2026-08-17, AND THE PAIR IS THE POINT. probes/edit_survival_probe.py asks the question the offload probe cannot: a ticket can pass its physics green while every line the apprentice wrote was thrown away and rewritten by CC — the offload buying nothing while reporting success, which is a hollow green (Law 8). It reads the driver's own drive records against the working tree and dispositions each driven piece survived | rewritten | discarded | not-applied, deduped on the drive's own identity because `enough` is a count. It does NOT collapse a mixture (Law 7): a drive whose files disagree is reported `mixed`, per-file carried whole, and the carrier names the HEAD the comparison was actually taken against — the spec says 'at the PROVED commit' and this reads the working tree, so naming the drift beats a second implementation that would have to be kept honest against the first. Same nexus, same five-piece population, same consumer, no authority.
traces_to: Law 1 — the resolver is spent on the novel, not on re-deriving the settled. A decompose piece plus its bounds plus its proof is a settled answer; typing it out with the most expensive model available is re-derivation, and this device is the structure that answer becomes.

Law 8 and its why — nothing enters proven-space without a proof a hollow build couldn't pass, BECAUSE a peer system requires trust where a hierarchy does not (Akien, 2026-08-16). This device's output is judged by exactly the gates CC's output is judged by; relaxing one to admit it would destroy the measurement, and a false green here would be leaned on by a peer.
Law 3 — nothing is known until measured. Whether the offload works is unmeasured, is labeled a hypothesis throughout this charter, and is answered by the probe rather than by this build.
Telos 1 — every call metered, because it rides the sole pipe like any other consumer and moves yield_report like any other consumer.
owner: CC owns this device's code and proofs and gates writes to them. Akien owns the intention and ruled the operating shape on 2026-08-15 (traffic through the inference proxy so we learn from it) and the consumer/provider split on 2026-08-16 ('the consumer asks for what it wants. period, end of story'), which is why this device composes and asks and the proxy knows nothing about it. He also owns the one thing this device cannot decide for itself: whether a runnable aider — 24 third-party packages including two telemetry clients — may be installed on his box.
gated_by_why: THE HANDS THIS INTENTION'S OWNER-GATE ADMITS — the machine-readable half of `owner` above, and the only half cairn.devices.harbor_master.clearance.clear() reads. CC alone, because the code and its proofs are CC's to gate; Akien's ownership is of the intention and is exercised by ruling, not by a clearance stamp.
proof: proofs/test_interceptor.py (15 teeth) — the eight-callable surface is complete, every exception name is catchable, no stray `*Error` attribute would break aider's dir() walk, the fallback exception list is checked against aider's own by AST, usage is never fabricated on a cache hit, and `installed()` is asserted in BOTH directions (True for ours, False for a foreign module at that name — the negative half is what carries falsifier clause 1). The touched-attribute set is required NON-EMPTY before it is required to be a subset, so a pass cannot be earned by nothing happening. proofs/test_fence.py (10 teeth) — a widened model and a widened PROVIDER are each refused before the host is touched (the injected door is a tripwire that raises if reached), the refusal is recorded verbatim and on disk, an on-fence ask is still ALLOWED (a fence that refuses everything is a wall, not a fence), the fence is exact-match against five near-misses, and the refusal is required to escape every except-handler parsed live out of aider's `simple_send_with_retries`. proofs/test_translation.py — every substantive span of a produced prompt traces to a berthed packet field (owed with piece 5). ALL TEETH WERE MUTATION-TESTED before the seal: 12 mutants injecting real defects (fence opened, fence fired late, refusal unrecorded, refusal absorbed, provider check removed, usage fabricated, surface shortened, stray *Error added, touched-recording blinded, identity check reduced to presence, state moved to class-space, exception list drifted) — 12 killed, and the two that survived the first round are why the last two teeth exist. All under the tester, netns, twice. proofs/test_driver.py (25 teeth) — the drive runs the REAL Coder behind the fence with a fixture resolver, the result is serializable, the repo map stays at 0, the ask cap holds, an undirected drive lands in the fence's own store, and the DRIVER ITSELF (not a restaging of it) reaches no network with a guaranteed-cold model cache. proofs/test_edit_survival_probe.py (16 teeth) — armed at the berth the ticket names (resolved against the repo root, not the CWD: the bare run was green and the netns run was red, and the sibling probe's identical tooth had been passing for a reason that was luck), each of the four dispositions distinct, a mixture reported `mixed`, the vocabulary proved a translation of driver.survival's own source, one drive appended twice still one drive, and `enough` unlowered by drives that applied nothing. MUTATION-TESTED at the seal: four mutants — hollow drive (8 teeth red), ask cap removed (1), in-venv model seed removed (1, naming the litellm URL), default ask-log resolution removed (1). Six proofs, green twice bare and sealed under netns.
provenance: Born 2026-08-15 from Akien's idea, captured verbatim: use aider via a shim as a build device running Qwen3-Coder-30B-Instruct (Q4_K_M) on hex to build tickets CC specifies. Cast the same day. The child ticket inference-domain-chat-verb was built and crossed PROVED on 2026-08-16 to supply the road this device drives on — and its build is where the design of THIS device was actually settled, twice by correction. First: a builder-aider row in the proxy's domains stack, carrying this device's model pin and money-fence, was authored and then killed by ruling — 'the consumer asks for what it wants' — which moved the whole fence obligation here and is why the fence is an object in this device rather than a row in that one. Second: the proof criterion written to protect that property was malformed (it forbade any proof from naming builder-aider, which is self-defeating, since proving an absence requires naming the absent thing), and the correction — 'how the fuck do we prove the thing itself then?' — is why this charter's falsifier names its own failure modes explicitly rather than gesturing at them. The chart chain for this build berthed 2026-08-16 across seven stages, validate at validate-20260816T175726-c9e861a39863. THE DRIVER LANDED 2026-08-17 under ticket aider-builds-a-piece, and it is the voyage that made the device measurable: the offload probe's population moved off zero for the first time in its life (1 shimmed ticket, 8 verdicts, all pass). Eight criteria answered by their instruments, eight hypotheses dispositioned — six confirmed, TWO KILLED, both by one shape of error: an expectation that named the ARRANGEMENT and not the code that uses it. Those two are filed edges (g) and (h), and each is now a scar in driver.py rather than a sentence in a retrospective. What the voyage did NOT deliver is a surviving edit — filed edge (i).
